rationale: bugs_open/315 PLAN decision D7, and it exists because THIS council refuted my own measurement last round. In round be85a6d3 I claimed 'exactly three live steps stamp a page deployed and all three are armed with deploy_result_field, so the stale-fingerprint hazard cannot arise today'. The guardian seat replied that the number was 'almost certainly measured with a top-level workflow.steps census — documented elsewhere on this platform as blind to actions nested inside sub_workflow/substeps', and asked for re-verification. It was right and it never saw my query. A RECURSIVE walk finds SIX stampers, of which THREE ARE UNARMED — page-rebuild, pageflow-builder and site-work-orchestrator, all at workflow.steps.<loop>.config.sub_workflow.steps.update_page_status, which are the page-BUILDING paths, i.e. the ones that actually emit new bytes. THE HAZARD: UpdatePageStatusAction writes pages.content_hash only when the deploy-evidence guard ran, so an unarmed step that deploys new bytes leaves the PREVIOUS deploy's fingerprint in place; the divergence check (DGH-015) then reports a healthy page as diverged, permanently, because nothing rewrites that row. This migration arms the three, which is what makes migration 526 (enabling the check) appliable — 526 gates on the recursive unarmed count being zero and currently refuses.

plan.summary: Arm the three remaining update_page_status steps that stamp 'deployed' without recording what was sent, by naming their sibling git_commit step's output_field (page_deployed) as deploy_result_field — mirroring migration 494's shape for the three agents it already armed. Plus its ROLLBACK sibling.

edits.rationale: NEW FILE. The config migration that closes the stale-fingerprint hazard and unblocks 526. Deliberately NOT a _HOLD file: deploy_result_field is ALREADY declared by the running binary (494 armed three other agents on 2026-08-20 and 232 fingerprints have been written since), so there is no image-before-config ordering constraint. Verified against the live fleet: v1.0.1322 / commit bac18992 contains the check, ancestry tested with a reverse-direction control, and the binary probed for the registered check name with a near-identical absent literal as the negative control.
edits.sketch: Three snapshot_agent() calls first. ALREADY-APPLIED gate: recursive count of the three agents' stamps already naming deploy_result_field = 3 -> RAISE '...already...'. COUNTED NEEDLE-GATE: exactly 3 agents must still have a loop sub_workflow pairing a git_commit step named deploy_page (output_field 'page_deployed') with a deployed-stamping update_page_status; anything else aborts rather than wiring a guard to a field nothing writes. Then two plain UPDATEs (jsonb_set into {workflow,steps,build_pages_loop,config,sub_workflow,steps,update_page_status,config,deploy_result_field} for page-rebuild + pageflow-builder, and {…,build_items_loop,…} for site-work-orchestrator — written explicitly rather than via one clever shared expression, because the loop step is named differently on the third and three plain statements review better than one that is right for reconstructable reasons). VERIFY AS A RAISE, not SELECTs (ON_ERROR_STOP does not fire on a non-empty result, so a SELECT-based verify cannot stop the COMMIT): assert all 3 armed with page_deployed, AND assert the FLEET-WIDE unarmed count is now 0 — the second is the one that matters, because it is exactly what 526 gates on and it catches a fourth stamper appearing meanwhile. BLAST RADIUS MEASURED: arming changes behaviour in exactly one case (the stamp is REFUSED when the deploy step reported a skip), so exposure is 'how often do these three run' — runs in ALL HISTORY: 0, 0 and 0; zero scheduled_tasks target them; zero site_work_items routed at them. REACHABILITY, which a run-count cannot answer: exactly ONE live dispatch reference fleet-wide, maintenance-triage carrying agent_type=page-rebuild — established by matching only VALUES at dispatch keys, because a substring search over default_config::text also hits council-gate, fix-proposer and domain-research-classifier, where the names are PROSE inside reviewer prompts rather than wiring. So this is inert today and protective the moment maintenance-triage routes anything at page-rebuild. ARM rather than DELETE deliberately: these are live definitions this lane does not own, and arming is the reversible half of that choice.

edits.rationale: NEW FILE. Restores the prior behaviour exactly: the three stamp 'deployed' without reading the deploy result and leave content_hash untouched.
edits.sketch: Snapshots, then `default_config #- '{…,deploy_result_field}'` on each of the two paths. Verify block asserts BOTH directions: (a) none of the three still names a deploy_result_field, and (b) THE THREE DEPLOYED-STAMPING STEPS STILL EXIST — because a rollback that removed the step or its config object would silently stop these agents marking pages deployed at all, which is far worse than the hazard being rolled back. Header warns that running it re-opens the hazard and that 526's gate will then refuse again (the intended interlock), and that if the check is already enabled it must be disabled too.

bugs_open/336: this lane armed stampers on 2026-08-20 and took every page-publish in the estate down for 33 minutes by verifying the config and never asking whether a page could still publish — hence the damage-query-first instruction in this file's header
Migration 494 (applied 2026-08-20): the shape this migration mirrors, and the evidence that deploy_result_field is already declared by the running binary — 232 fingerprints written since
plan.risks: Behaviourally inert today by measurement (0 runs in all history for all three), and the single behaviour change when they DO run is the intended one: refuse the 'deployed' stamp when the deploy step reported a skip, instead of stamping regardless — which is the defect bugs_open/315 exists to fix. Failure mode if evidence cannot be resolved is FAIL-OPEN by design (stamp anyway, log DEPLOY_EVIDENCE_UNREADABLE at warning), so a mistake here produces noise, not a stall. The 33-minute outage this lane caused on 2026-08-20 was a StrictConfig rejection of an UNDECLARED key; that key is now declared and proven live by three armed agents and 232 fingerprints, so that specific failure cannot recur here. Not held: no image-before-config constraint applies. WHAT I AM LESS SURE OF, stated: (1) reachability rests on a dispatch-key value scan — if an agent reaches page-rebuild by a mechanism that stores the name somewhere other than a value at a key I matched, my 'one live reference' undercounts, though that only makes arming MORE useful, not less; (2) I have not observed any of these three actually run, so the armed path is unexercised on them — the header therefore directs the applier to the damage query first rather than to the benefit.
